links.title: SPIEval: Evaluating Large Language Models as Mobile Assistants over Scattered Personal Information

evidence: Section 3.3 describes human curation, cross-validation, and gold-answer verification for 250 tasks over 4,335 records and 10 apps.
Section 5 reports best model GPT-5.5 (xhigh) at 57.3% and weakest at 16.4% across nine LLMs.
Section 6 analyzes failure modes and retrieval behavior, including 79% failures from incorrect parameter values and <2% advanced retrieval use.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Highly relevant LLM agent/tool-use/retrieval evaluation benchmark with moderate novelty as a synthetic mobile personal-information benchmark; moderately rigorous human curation and controlled evaluation, though claims rely on self-reported results with some table/figure inconsistencies and no explicit limitations.

primary_link.title: SPIEval: Evaluating Large Language Models as Mobile Assistants over Scattered Personal Information

top5.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as mobile assistants, where a key challenge is leveraging personal information scattered across multiple applications (apps) to complete user instructions. However, due to the lack of dedicated benchmarks, their capabilities remain poorly understood. To address this gap, we introduce SPIEval, a human-curated benchmark grounded in five cognitive capabilities (i.e., reasoning, disambiguation, integration, preference inference, and multi-intent decomposition). SPIEval comprises 250 tasks spanning 4,335 personal records distributed across 10 apps and supports multi-turn interaction through 21 tools. Analysis shows that the benchmark exhibits diverse scenarios, challenging tasks, scattered information, controllable environments, and verifiable outcomes. We evaluate nine representative LLMs and find substantial room for improvement. The best-performing model, GPT-5.5 (xhigh), achieves only 57.3% accuracy, while the weakest achieves just 16.4%. Further analysis reveals that 79% of failures stem from inaccurate information localization, as LLMs often commit to plausible but incorrect information instead of continuing retrieval for verification. We also find that fewer than 2% of retrieval actions employ advanced search methods and observe substantial variation in search efficiency across models. These findings expose fundamental limitations of current LLM-based mobile assistants and motivate future research in this direction. Data and code are available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/Junjie-Ye/SPIEval.
top5.summary_zh: 本文提出 SPIEval，一個由人工建構的評測基準，用於評估大型語言模型（LLM）在行動助理情境中，運用分散於多個應用程式之個人資訊來完成使用者指令的能力。研究動機在於現有評測多假設必要資訊已明確提供，而真實情境中資訊往往分散於不同應用程式，現有方法難以反映此挑戰。SPIEval 涵蓋五種認知能力：推理、消歧、整合、偏好推斷與多意圖分解，共 250 個任務，對應 10 個應用程式中 4,335 筆個人記錄，並提供 21 個工具以支援多輪互動。評估結果顯示，表現最佳的 GPT-5.5（xhigh）僅達 57.3% 準確率，最弱模型僅 16.4%，顯示當前 LLM 在此任務上仍有大幅進步空間。進一步分析指出，79% 的失敗源於資訊定位不準確，模型常在找到看似合理但不正確的資訊後便停止檢索，而非持續驗證；此外，僅不到 2% 的檢索動作使用進階搜尋方法。這些發現揭示目前 LLM 行動助理的根本限制，並指出未來改進方向。SPIEval 提供可控環境與可驗證結果，為此領域建立嚴謹的評測基準。

links.title: Whose Refusal Is It? The Unmeasured Contribution of Black-Box Multimodal Guardrails

evidence: §4.1 reports exact-match guard blocks vs judge-scored model refusals, with guard share ranging from 0% to 99% across the three read settings.

§4.2 Table 2 shows text-only guards dropping from 100/100 and 81/100 blocks to 0/100 when the same unencoded harmful payload moves from text to image, while a multimodal guard blocks 99/100 in both channels.
§4.6 Table 6 reports deployable vs granted protocol differences, including a -63pp granted effect that becomes -3pp and non-significant when deployable.
§4.8 Table 9 isolates read position inside ECSO, finding SAFE answer regeneration carries -18pp and -26pp while TELL and CAP stage grants are not significant.
§4.16 describes a designed end-to-end replicate of the protocol grid and drift band of 0-10pp, with architecture-ordered inflation reproducing across campaigns.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Strongly relevant to AI safety, red-teaming/evaluation, and multimodal guardrails. The paper contributes a novel decomposition of defended-pipeline refusals into guard vs model refusals and shows evaluation-protocol artifacts can manufacture large apparent safety benefits. It reports quantitative exact-match counts, McNemar tests, multi-judge checks, a designed replicate, multiplicity control, and explicit limitations. Generalizability is deliberately constrained to specific defenses, targets, and encodings, and several findings rely on small or single-model cells, so magnitudes should not transfer. Reproducibility is strong via detailed artifacts and implementation disclosure. Assessment is based only on the supplied document, treated as untrusted data.

primary_link.title: Whose Refusal Is It? The Unmeasured Contribution of Black-Box Multimodal Guardrails

A defended pipeline holds two components that can refuse (the guardrail, and the target model out of its own alignment), and every reported metric is a sum over both. We show that the guardrail's actual share of the safety credited to it runs from none of it to essentially all of it, decided by two variables no evaluation records: which channel carries the payload, and what text the harness places in
top5.summary_zh: 本文探討黑箱防護欄（guardrail）在防禦管線中實際貢獻的安全性比例。作者指出，防禦管線中防護欄與目標模型皆可能拒絕有害請求，傳統攻擊成功率指標無法區分兩者貢獻。透過將防護欄阻擋（以固定拒答字串精確匹配）與模型自身拒答（以評判模型判讀）分離，他們發現防護欄的貢獻範圍可從0%到99%，取決於兩個未被記錄的變數：承載惡意內容的通道（文字或影像），以及評測時提供給防護欄內部讀取的文字（編碼攻擊或未編碼原始請求）。實驗顯示，僅文字防護欄對影像通道完全失明，而多模態防護欄雖能補足覆蓋，但在對抗性困難的正常流量上鑑別力較弱，因此建議以通道路由部署而非取代。此外，評測時若將未編碼請求提供給防護欄，會顯著高估其效益，且此效應主要由生成答案的階段而非決策階段所承載。作者亦修正自身先前的研究數據。主要限制在於結果基於特定防護欄、模型與攻擊編碼，通用性有限。此研究強調評估協議透明化的重要性，以免數字失真。
